title: How do you build a training matrix for aged care?
description: How to build an aged care training matrix: screening gates, core matters, aide in-service hours and evidence under Australian and US aged care rules, by role.
shortAnswer: An aged care training matrix is built by treating screening and qualification as entry gates, then mapping each care role against the training its service type requires: in Australia, the Aged Care Act 2024 and strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards; in the United States, the CMS rules for nursing homes, home health aides and hospice aides. Each cell records the frequency, the trigger and the record a regulator or surveyor will check.
keyTakeaways: Start with gates, not courses. Worker screening in Australia and aide competency evaluation in the United States must be satisfied before a person delivers care.
The service type decides the rows. Australian registration categories and US provider types (nursing home, home health, hospice) carry different training duties.
Volunteers and contractors are workers for these rules, so they need rows and records like employees.
Australia's Outcome 2.9 lists core matters for regular competency based training, and several systems need training at least annually.
US nurse aides, home health aides and hospice aides all need at least 12 hours of in-service training a year, but their entry routes and supervision differ.

sections.heading: What does an aged care training matrix have to prove?

blocks.text: It has to prove that every person delivering care was screened, holds the qualifications or skills the role needs, has been trained on the matters the regulator names, and is still current today. Aged care differs from most sectors because older people receiving care are often cognitively impaired, so the rules put unusual weight on who is allowed near them and on abuse prevention, dementia care and incident reporting.

This guide applies the method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) to two markets covered in this library: Australia, under the [Aged Care Act 2024](/regulations/aged-care-act-2024-worker-obligations) and the [strengthened Aged Care Quality Standards](/regulations/aged-care-quality-standards-training), and the United States, under the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) rules for [nursing homes](/regulations/cms-nursing-home-training-requirements), [home health aides](/regulations/home-health-aide-training-requirements) and [hospice aides](/regulations/hospice-aide-training-requirements). The Australian Act and Standards have been in force since November 1, 2025.

The Australian rule on training is stated plainly in Outcome 2.9 of the Aged Care Rules: "The provider must provide aged care workers with training and supervision to enable them to effectively perform their roles."

sections.heading: Who counts as a worker on an aged care matrix?

blocks.text: Everyone who delivers or supports care for the provider, including volunteers and contractors. Under section 11(4) of the Aged Care Act 2024, an aged care worker includes individuals employed or engaged, including volunteers, by a registered provider, and a note confirms independent contractors are included. The Aged Care Quality and Safety Commission's guidance expects training records for all workers, including contractors.

US rules reach just as wide. 42 CFR 483.95 requires a nursing home training program for all new and existing staff, contractors and volunteers, consistent with their roles. Hospices must orient employees and contracted staff who have patient and family contact, and train volunteers consistent with hospice industry standards.

Two further groups need their own rows in Australia. Responsible persons, such as directors and senior managers, must be screened, and section 180 of the Act sets a due diligence duty that includes acquiring and maintaining knowledge. Registered nurses are also critical to residential rows, because section 175 requires a registered nurse on site at all times.

sections.heading: How does the type of service change the rows?

blocks.text: The service type decides which frameworks apply, so record it at the top of each role group before assigning obligations. The table summarizes what the library's regulation pages record for each setting.

sections.heading: Which aged care rows are gates rather than refreshers?

blocks.text: Screening, qualification and aide competency evaluation are gates: until they are met, the person should not deliver care, so the matrix status must block rostering rather than simply show 'due'. Treat these rows differently from annual refreshers.

items: **Australian worker screening.** Under Rules 152-20 and 152-25, the current routes are a police certificate no more than 3 years old without disqualifying convictions, an NDIS clearance, a pending check with supervision and a statutory declaration, or supervised school work experience. Record the certificate date so the 3 year limit can be tracked.
**Australian qualifications.** Rule 152-35 requires workers to have appropriate qualifications, skills or experience. Record which one the provider relied on for each role.
**US aide competency evaluation.** Home health and hospice aides must pass an RN competency evaluation before furnishing services, with certain skills observed on a patient or pseudo-patient.

**US break in service.** A home health or hospice aide who goes 24 consecutive months without providing compensated aide services must complete a new training and competency program, so the matrix should flag long gaps, not only expiry dates.

**Professional registration.** For nurses in Australia, registration renewal is due by 31 May each year under the [Ahpra registration standards](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards). The matrix checks the national register; it does not track the nurse's 20 hours of CPD, which the nurse declares to the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia.

sections.heading: What will an aged care auditor or surveyor ask to see?

blocks.text: Records that show each worker's screening, qualifications and training against their role, kept for the required period. In Australia, Rule 154-905 sets the contents of worker records and Rule 154-910 requires seven year retention, and the Commission rates providers against each outcome at audit. The Commission's own guidance refers to a training matrix by role type and gives palliative care, infection prevention and control lead, and fire warden or first aider training as examples.

items: **Demonstrated competence.** Action 2.9.6 asks for competency based training, and the model psychosocial hazards Code says it is not sufficient to tell a worker about a procedure and ask them to acknowledge it ([psychosocial hazards](/regulations/psychosocial-hazards-training-requirements)). Use observed or tested assessment, such as [verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency), for care tasks.

**Repeated, not one off, training on conduct.** The Australian Human Rights Commission's positive duty guidelines say one off induction training has proven ineffective unless periodically reinforced, and list attendance records with a copy of the content as evidence ([positive duty](/regulations/positive-duty-sexual-harassment-training)).

**Privacy handling.** The Office of the Australian Information Commissioner describes staff training as an organizational security measure under APP 11, relevant to anyone handling residents' records ([Privacy Act training](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)).

**First aid coverage.** Regulation 42 of the model WHS Regulations requires an adequate number of trained first aiders; Victoria applies its own compliance code ([first aid](/regulations/first-aid-training-requirements-australia)).
**US facility assessment.** CMS ties the amount and type of nursing home training to the facility assessment, which must be documented and reviewed at least annually. Surveyors can compare the two.
**US hospice in-service.** Hospices must keep a written description of in-service training provided in the previous 12 months.

blocks.text: Keep CPR and fire safety as provider rows for registered nurses too: the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia excludes routine annual CPR and mandatory fire training from what counts as CPD. For record handling across rows, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: Why should each aged care row have a named owner?

blocks.text: Because liability sits with individuals as well as the provider. In Australia, workers and responsible persons who fail to comply with the Aged Care Code of Conduct face civil penalties of 250 penalty units under sections 173 and 174, and the Code requires services to be delivered "in a safe and competent manner, with care and skill". A named owner for each requirement keeps content current, and a named owner for each role keeps the people in it current.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each aged care matrix row to the outcome, rule or regulation that requires it and to the assessment that evidences it, so a change to the Standards or a CMS rule shows which roles and records it affects. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance) and [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Which core matters must Australian aged care training cover?
faqs.a: Action 2.9.6 of the strengthened Standards lists person centred, rights based care; culturally safe, trauma aware and healing informed care; dementia; medical emergencies; and the Code of Conduct, the Serious Incident Response Scheme and the Quality Standards. Providers decide how often to refresh each, so the matrix should record that policy interval.

faqs.q: Do US nursing homes need annual training for every topic?
faqs.a: Not for every topic. 42 CFR 483.95 lists required topics for all staff and bases the amount and type of training on the facility assessment. Nurse aides need at least 12 hours of in-service a year, and operators with five or more facilities need annual compliance and ethics training.

faqs.q: Can a new aged care worker start before their police check returns?
faqs.a: Under the Aged Care Rules, a pending check is one of the screening routes, but only with supervision and a statutory declaration. The matrix should record the supervision arrangement and the date the check was lodged, and block unsupervised rostering until the result is held.

faqs.q: How long must aged care training records be kept?
faqs.a: In Australia, Rule 154-910 requires worker records to be kept for seven years. In the United States, record periods depend on the rule; for example, OSHA bloodborne pathogens training records must be kept for 3 years. Use the longest period that applies to each record.
